questions.question: How many players does each team start the match with on the pitch?
questions.explanation: Eleven per side at kick-off, not counting substitutes.

questions.question: How long does an official match last without extra time?
questions.explanation: Two halves of 45 minutes each.

questions.question: How many referees are on the pitch during a match?
questions.explanation: One centre referee assisted by two linesmen.

questions.question: What colour is the card that means an immediate sending-off?
questions.explanation: It means leaving the pitch at once with no substitute.

questions.question: What does a yellow card mean?
questions.explanation: Two yellow cards in a match mean a sending-off.

questions.question: Who is the only player allowed to touch the ball with their hands during play?
questions.explanation: And only inside their own penalty area.

questions.question: What is the kick taken from the corner of the pitch called?
questions.explanation: Awarded when a defender puts the ball out over their own goal line.

questions.question: What is the ball being returned to play with both hands from behind the touchline called?
questions.explanation: Taken with both hands from behind the head.

questions.question: What happens if two teams are level in a knockout match after extra time?
questions.explanation: Five kicks each, then sudden-death kicks if it's still level.

questions.question: How many halves are there in a match?
questions.explanation: With a half-time break of no more than fifteen minutes.

questions.question: From what distance is a penalty kick taken?
questions.explanation: Eleven metres from the centre of the goal line.

questions.question: What does VAR stand for?
questions.explanation: Video Assistant Referee.

questions.question: How long does extra time last in knockout matches?
questions.explanation: Two extra periods of 15 minutes each.

questions.question: How many kicks does each team take in the initial round of a penalty shoot-out?
questions.explanation: Five kicks each, then it continues kick for kick.

questions.question: What is the official called who manages substitutions and shows the added time board?
questions.explanation: Sits between the two technical areas and handles administrative matters.

questions.question: When is a goal kick awarded?
options: When the ball goes out off a defender
When the ball crosses the goal line off an attacker
On a foul inside the area
questions.explanation: If it goes out off a defender instead, the opponent gets a corner.

questions.question: What is the difference between a direct and an indirect free kick?
options: The direct one needs two players
The indirect one is closer to goal
A goal can be scored straight from the direct one
questions.explanation: An indirect kick must touch another player before a goal can count.

questions.question: How many metres must the wall stand back from the ball at a free kick?
questions.explanation: Equal to ten yards in the imperial system.

questions.question: What is the area set aside for the manager and coaching staff called?
questions.explanation: It may not be left without the referee's permission.

questions.question: What is the decision when a defender deliberately handles the ball inside their own penalty area?
questions.explanation: With a possible card too, depending on the nature of the handball.

questions.question: What is the circumference of a regulation football, roughly?
questions.explanation: Under FIFA's rules for a size 5 ball.

questions.question: What is the regulation width of the goal?
questions.explanation: Eight yards between the posts.

questions.question: What is the regulation height of the goal?
questions.explanation: Eight feet from the ground to the crossbar.

questions.question: When is a player not considered offside?
options: When standing in the opponents' half
When receiving the ball from a throw-in
questions.explanation: There's also no offside from a goal kick or a corner kick.

questions.question: Can a player be offside in their own half?
options: Only if they touch the ball
questions.explanation: Offside requires the player to be in the opponents' half.

questions.question: In 2022, how many substitutions per team were made permanent for top-level competitions?
questions.explanation: The number had been raised from three to five as a temporary measure during the 2020 pandemic.

questions.question: What is the body responsible for setting football's laws called?
questions.explanation: The International Football Association Board.

questions.question: How many official Laws of the Game are there?
questions.explanation: The first version of the laws, in the 19th century, had only thirteen.

questions.question: What is the "back-pass rule"?
options: The keeper may not pick up a deliberate pass from a teammate's foot
Passing is banned in extra time
The keeper may not come off their line
questions.explanation: Introduced in 1992 to stop time-wasting.

questions.question: How many seconds is a goalkeeper allowed to hold the ball in their hands?
questions.explanation: The limit rose from six to eight seconds in July 2025, and going over it gives the opponent a corner kick.

questions.question: What is the regulation pitch length for international matches?
questions.explanation: The width ranges from 64 to 75 metres.

questions.question: What is the radius of the centre circle?
questions.explanation: The same distance opponents must keep from the ball at free kicks.

questions.question: How deep is the penalty area from the goal line?
questions.explanation: 18 yards, which is where the nickname "the 18-yard box" comes from.

questions.question: How deep is the six-yard box?
questions.explanation: Six yards, hence the name "the six-yard box".

questions.question: When does the referee use VAR to review a decision?
options: For goals, penalties, red cards and mistaken identity
questions.explanation: In 2026 reviews were extended to red cards from a clearly wrong second yellow card.

questions.question: What is the decision if the ball hits the referee and decisively changes the course of play?
questions.explanation: A rule added in 2019 to deal with this situation.

questions.question: What is a "dropped ball"?
options: A ball the referee drops to restart play
A ball that goes out of play
A shot that hits the crossbar
A high ball in the air
questions.explanation: Now given to the team that had possession when play stopped.

questions.question: What does the "advantage rule" mean in refereeing?
options: Giving the stronger team a decision
Letting play continue if stopping it would hurt the fouled team
questions.explanation: The referee signals it by throwing both arms forward.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of players needed for a match to continue?
questions.explanation: If either team drops below seven, the match is abandoned.

questions.question: What happens if a player scores an own goal directly from a throw-in?
questions.explanation: A goal can never be scored directly from a throw-in, at either end.

questions.question: When were coloured cards first used at a World Cup?
questions.explanation: The first yellow card went to a Soviet player in the opening match against Mexico.

questions.question: Who came up with the idea of coloured cards?
questions.explanation: He got the idea from traffic lights while driving.

questions.question: In what year was the rule banning the keeper from picking up a teammate's pass introduced?
questions.explanation: After the 1990 World Cup, which suffered from a slow pace of play.

questions.question: What was the "golden goal" rule, scrapped in 2004?
options: A decisive goal in a shoot-out
A goal that counted as two
A goal from a free kick
The first goal in extra time ended the match
questions.explanation: Scrapped because it made teams play far too cautiously.

questions.question: What was the short-lived "silver goal" rule?
options: A goal from outside the area
A goal that counted as half a point
The match ended at the break in extra time if a team was ahead
questions.explanation: Applied briefly in the early 2000s, then scrapped.

questions.question: What is the decision if a player touches the ball with their hand unintentionally and then scores from it?
questions.explanation: Any handball immediately before a goal rules it out, even if accidental.

questions.question: Under the modern laws, when does a handball count as an offence?
options: When the arm is in an unnatural position that makes the body bigger
questions.explanation: Arm position is now the test, replacing the old intent-based standard.

questions.question: How many players must be between an attacker and the goal line to avoid offside?
questions.explanation: Usually the keeper and one defender — any two players will do.

questions.question: Is an attacker offside if they are level with the second-last defender?
options: Only if they touch the ball
questions.explanation: Being level is not offside.

questions.question: What is "semi-automated offside technology"?
options: A camera tracking system that calls offside automatically
A chip inside a player's boot
questions.explanation: First widely used at the 2022 World Cup.

questions.question: At which major tournament was goal-line technology first used?
questions.explanation: After the controversy over Lampard's disallowed goal in 2010.

questions.question: What is the decision when a player celebrates by taking off their shirt?
questions.explanation: A mandatory caution, whatever the reason for the celebration.

questions.question: What is the decision when a player runs into the crowd to celebrate?
questions.explanation: Considered unsporting behaviour, which draws a caution.

questions.question: What does "denying an obvious goal-scoring opportunity" mean in refereeing?
options: A foul that usually means a sending-off
questions.explanation: Reduced to a caution if the foul was an attempt to play the ball inside the area.

questions.question: When may a goalkeeper move on the goal line during a penalty shoot-out?
options: They must keep one foot on or above the line at the moment of the kick
They may not move at all
They may step forward two metres
They may come off the line after the shot
questions.explanation: A rule adjusted to make it easier to apply with video technology.

questions.question: What is the decision if the penalty taker touches the ball twice in a row?
options: Indirect free kick to the opponents
questions.explanation: The taker may not touch the ball again before another player does.

questions.question: How many players are needed to take a passed penalty kick?
questions.explanation: Allowed, provided the teammate is outside the area when it's taken.

questions.question: What is the decision if the assistant referee raises the flag for offside and the review overturns it?
options: The call is overturned and play restarts from the point of intervention
questions.explanation: Because play had already been stopped, it restarts with a dropped ball.

questions.question: Why do assistant referees sometimes delay raising the offside flag?
options: To let the attack finish before it's reviewed
questions.explanation: So a valid goal isn't wasted.

questions.question: What is the decision when a player deliberately wastes time at a throw-in?
questions.explanation: Considered unsporting behaviour.

questions.question: What is the official ball size for senior matches?
questions.explanation: Size 4 is used at youth level.

questions.question: What is the regulation weight of the ball at kick-off?
questions.explanation: The specification for a size 5 ball.

questions.question: What happens if the ball bursts during a shot that ends up in the net?
options: The goal is disallowed and play restarts with a dropped ball
questions.explanation: The ball is out of play the instant it bursts.

questions.question: Can a goal be scored directly from a goal kick?
questions.explanation: If it goes into the taker's own goal instead, the opponent gets a corner.

questions.question: Can a goal be scored directly from a corner kick?
questions.explanation: Law 17 allows it, but only into the opposing team's goal.

questions.question: What is a goal scored directly from a corner kick called?
questions.explanation: Named after Argentina's Cesáreo Onzari scored one in 1924.

questions.question: Can a goal be scored directly from the kick-off at the centre of the pitch?
questions.explanation: Allowed since the laws were amended, though hard to achieve in practice.

questions.question: When is a red card shown for "violent conduct"?
options: For using excessive force that endangers an opponent's safety
questions.explanation: Safety is the test, not the outcome of the challenge.

questions.question: What is the decision if a player spits at an opponent?
questions.explanation: One of the most serious offences in the laws of the game.

questions.question: Can the goalkeeper handle the ball after a throw-in from a teammate?
options: Only after another player touches it
questions.explanation: A throw-in from a teammate is covered by the same back-pass rule.

questions.question: When did the modern offside rule — level is not offside — come into force?
questions.explanation: A change made after the Italy World Cup to encourage attacking play.

questions.question: When was the tackle from behind strictly banned?
questions.explanation: The penalty was toughened to a straight red card to protect players.

questions.question: Which goal-line technology system uses a magnetic field instead of cameras?
questions.explanation: GoalRef detects coils inside the ball via a magnetic field, while Hawk-Eye and GoalControl rely on cameras.

questions.question: How many cameras does a goal-line technology system typically use per goal?
questions.explanation: Seven high-speed cameras per goal in the most common system.

questions.question: Where does the referee review a decision using video technology?
options: A pitchside monitor near the technical area
On the big screen in the stadium
questions.explanation: Known as the referee review area, off-limits to everyone else.

questions.question: Who has the final say when video technology is used?
questions.explanation: The video room only advises; the decision stays with the on-field referee.

questions.question: What is the decision if an outsider enters the pitch and affects a goal?
options: The goal is disallowed and play restarts with a dropped ball
questions.explanation: Outside interference is treated as voiding the passage of play.

questions.question: What is the decision if a player scores with their hand unseen by the referee and the match carries on?
questions.explanation: The referee's decisions on matters of fact are final once the match has ended.

questions.question: What is the maximum width for the pitch markings?
questions.explanation: And every line must be the same width.

questions.question: Are the lines considered part of the area they mark out?
questions.explanation: So the ball is only out of play once it has fully crossed the line.

questions.question: When is the ball considered out of play?
options: When it has fully crossed the line
When a player touches it while outside
Only when the referee blows the whistle
questions.explanation: The ball must cross the line entirely, whether on the ground or in the air.

questions.question: What is the arc-shaped marking outside the penalty area called?
questions.explanation: It marks the distance other players must stand behind at a penalty kick.

questions.question: What is the small mark outside the pitch near the corner flag for?
options: To mark how far defenders must stand back at a corner kick
questions.explanation: It helps the referee judge the 9.15-metre distance quickly.

questions.question: Can the goalkeeper swap with another player during a match?
questions.explanation: Any player can swap roles with the keeper after telling the referee.

questions.question: What is the decision if two players swap the goalkeeper's role without informing the referee?
options: Indirect free kick to the opponents
A caution for both players once play stops
questions.explanation: It's an administrative offence and doesn't void the play.

questions.question: Is jewellery allowed during a match?
options: No jewellery at all is allowed
questions.explanation: For safety reasons — taping it up isn't enough.

questions.question: What is the rule on the colour of a player's thermal base layer?
options: It must match the shirt sleeve's main colour
questions.explanation: To avoid visual confusion during play.

questions.question: When may the referee abandon a match for good?
options: By a decision of the crowd
At their own discretion, for safety reasons or outside interference
questions.explanation: The referee's authority on this is absolute within the laws.

questions.question: What is the decision if a player throws a boot or object at the ball?
options: A direct free kick or penalty kick, plus a card
questions.explanation: Treated as if the ball had been touched unfairly.

questions.question: What is the maximum length of the half-time break?
questions.explanation: It may not be extended without the referee's agreement.

questions.question: In what year were the first laws of football drawn up?
questions.explanation: Alongside the founding of the Football Association in London.

questions.question: In what year was the International Football Association Board founded?
questions.explanation: Eighteen years before FIFA was founded.

questions.question: How many votes does FIFA hold in IFAB's votes on rule changes?
questions.explanation: Four votes, against one each for the four British associations.

questions.question: How many votes are needed to pass a change to the laws of the game?
questions.explanation: Meaning FIFA alone cannot push a change through.

questions.question: When was the penalty kick introduced into the laws of the game?
questions.explanation: Added to punish fouls near the goal.

questions.question: When were goalkeepers restricted to handling the ball inside the penalty area only?
questions.explanation: Before that, a keeper could use their hands anywhere in their own half.

questions.question: When was the offside rule changed from three defenders to two?
questions.explanation: The change led to a big rise in the goals-per-game rate.

questions.question: When were nets first used on goals officially?
questions.explanation: To settle disputes over whether the ball had crossed the line.

questions.question: When were substitutions first permitted in official matches?
questions.explanation: It began with one substitution for injury, then gradually expanded.

questions.question: When was the penalty shoot-out adopted to decide matches internationally?
questions.explanation: Before that, matches were settled by a replay or a draw of lots.
